$comment: One SDK for the whole tree. The 10.0 SDK builds every target here: net8.0 (the pure core and
the client), net8.0-windows (the add-in shim) and the suite's net8.0/net10.0 pair.
The shim compiles against Revit 2025's API, NOT the newest installed. Autodesk's floors are
Revit 2025 and 2026 on .NET 8 and Revit 2027 on .NET 10, and one net8.0-windows assembly loads
in all three. The reverse does not hold, and the compiler says so: a net8.0 project referencing
Revit 2027's RevitAPI.dll fails with CS1705 ('uses System.Runtime 10.0.0.0 which has a higher
version'). So the API version is what pins support, and pointing RevitApiDir at a newer install
rollForward latestFeature keeps this on 10.0.x: a machine with a newer 10.0 patch band builds
without editing this file, and a machine with only 8/9 fails loudly instead of silently
